extractions.description: Introduces and experimentally evaluates MOSAD, a multi-head model for open-set multivariate time-series anomaly detection, against supervised and unsupervised baselines on industrial and biomedical time-series datasets.

type.quote: Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets establish MOSAD as a new state-of-the-art in the TSAD field.
type.justification: The paper proposes a model and evaluates it experimentally on three datasets.

name.quote: Time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) is the field of identifying patterns that deviate from the expected behavior within the time-series
name.justification: This is the principal research field advanced by the paper.

name.quote: Recently, open-set anomaly detection (OSAD) methods are proposed to leverage a limited number of anomalous samples
name.justification: The paper extends open-set anomaly detection to multivariate time series.

name.quote: It is important to note that OSAD is different from the research fields of open-set recognition (OSR) [5] and out-of-distribution detection (OOD) [32].
name.justification: These fields are discussed as related but distinct context.
